claim: For every non-singleton Boolean polytope P, the supremal all-support exact-mean radius R(P) under rational unit-Euclidean-column feature matrices is at least k(P), the maximum support size of an actual edge.
quantifiers: Choose a maximum-support actual edge [u,v], a rational t in (0,1/2), y=(1-t)u+tv, and the one-row matrix a_j=sign(v_j-u_j) on the edge support and 0 elsewhere. Every exact-mean law at y is forced onto u,v and has radius (1-t)k(P); take the supremum as t decreases to 0.

inputs.supplied: Explicit or oracle-described Boolean polytope and a selected maximum-support edge for the proof witness.
inputs.acquired: No algorithmic edge acquisition is claimed.

proof: Exposed-face support argument and exact rational one-row calculation; runnable finite fixtures cover segments and the three-cube.
costs: One feature row, O(n) rational entries, and O(log denominator(t)) target bits; maximum-edge discovery is outside the existential statement.
baseline: P-round records the weaker midpoint lower bound k(P)/2.
falsifier: An exact-mean law at a relative-interior point of an exposed Boolean edge with positive mass outside that edge.
unresolved: External review and priority are unknown; this improves only the lower-bound constant and does not improve the upper bound.

claim: Given a Boolean polytope P with supplied actual-edge support upper bound k, rational A with Euclidean column norms at most 1, rational y in P, and any rational cost c, the candidate trajectory returns a Boolean vertex b in the minimal face F_P(y) with c^T(b-y)<=0 and ||A(b-y)||_infinity < B(k)<=1161k; for matroid bases k=2 and B=2209.
quantifiers: Uniform over all legal rational inputs, all rational costs, and all positive-atom outputs produced by the subsequent exact-mean law.

inputs.supplied: Rational A,y,c, a certified upper bound k, and either exact strong rational optimization/separation for general P or an independence oracle with exact submodular minimization for matroid specialization.
inputs.acquired: Per-state face, line-endpoint, rational derivative, shifted-Hessian direction, and affine-slice repair computations are part of the proposed algorithm.

proof: Supplied P-round derivation uses face-preserving spectral potential and negative curvature. Independent leaf audit reconstructed the restricted diagonal-trace lemma; no complete rational trajectory was executed.
costs: Polynomial query and bit bounds are claimed. Conservative step cap is about 1.79e49 for k=2,n=17. General actual-edge support acquisition is not included.
baseline: Berczi-Liu-Reis-Tarnawski Theorem 10 for nonnegative sparse matroid features; recent Komlos signers for unconstrained cube midpoint only.
falsifier: A failure of the strict-curvature direction, exact face/cost endpoint, displacement-based repair invariant, cumulative potential accounting, or final favorable response on a legal input.
unresolved: Full proof-to-implementation replay, independent external proof review, practical constants, and novelty/priority.

claim: For fixed rational A,y and good set G of Boolean vertices in F_P(y), a total oracle returning b in G with c^T(b-y)<=0 for every rational cost c suffices to construct an exact-mean law on G with at most dim(F_P(y))+1 atoms.
quantifiers: Fixed legal rational A,y and fixed discrepancy threshold; oracle responds to every rational separating cost used by the algorithm.

inputs.supplied: Good-set membership plus favorable response for each cost; rational target y=a/Q.
inputs.acquired: Ellipsoid transcript, exact infeasibility certificate, and affine-dependence reduction.

proof: Rational separation/ellipsoid transcript rules out a separator for the collected good vertices; exact LP yields the mean law.
costs: O(n^3(log Q+log n)) favorable responses; weights have O(log Q+n log n) bits.
falsifier: A legal total favorable-response oracle for which the transcript terminates without a convex combination of mean y, or a separator bit bound exceeding polynomial size.
unresolved: The favorable-good response routine must itself be implemented; ordinary P optimization is not a direct substitute.

claim: For every x in a strongly base-orderable matroid base polytope, Ercan arXiv:2609.38228v1 claims a law on vertices of the minimal face with EZ=x, a joint convex-order comparison, and every-outcome feature error below d R_m; with unit feature columns d<=2 and R_m<6.8383231851485.
quantifiers: Every finite strongly base-orderable matroid, legal feature matrix, and feasible mean x; d is the maximum feature norm of an available single exchange in the face.

inputs.supplied: Strong base-orderability and the legal feature map; source proof uses simultaneous complementary exchanges.
inputs.acquired: No polynomial-time strong-ordering witness acquisition or sampler is supplied in the source interface checked here.

proof: Source Theorem 5.1 and Corollary 5.2 use a hard signing law for simultaneous exchange families, dyadic approximation, and compactness.
costs: Existence-level law; no polynomial query or bit algorithm is established. Brute-force rational recovery by enumerating bases may require binomial(n,r) queries.
baseline: P-round candidate gives 2209 for matroid bases; Ercan source claim gives <13.676647 for the strongly base-orderable subclass.
falsifier: A strongly base-orderable instance violating the source theorem's pairwise exchange hypotheses or an exact dual witness against its asserted convex-order law.
unresolved: Source correctness/priority and finite-bit polynomial-time compilation.

claim: Exact marginals, negative dependence, or subgaussian tails alone do not imply an all-positive-support feature discrepancy bound independent of n.
quantifiers: On the n-cube, y=(1/2)^n, A is the all-ones row, and the independent Bernoulli law is an exact-marginal negatively dependent law with positive mass on 0^n and 1^n.

inputs.supplied: Explicit cube, exact mean, one unit-norm feature per column.

proof: The two extreme outcomes have discrepancy n/2 exactly.
costs: O(n) entries; no sampling computation is needed for the identity.
baseline: Pipage/swap rounding gives concentration but not this stronger support-wise guarantee.
falsifier: The explicit extreme support points fail the computed discrepancy, which is an exact arithmetic check.
unresolved: This refutes only inference from the stated dependence/tail properties, not the existence of a different good exact-mean law.

claim: Graph girth and spectrum alone imply a logarithmic cutoff for evaluation-matroid relations under arbitrary vertex labels.
quantifiers: For any fixed Boolean degree r and sufficiently many vertices, injectively label the graph while including all points of an affine (r+1)-flat in F_2^m.

inputs.supplied: Graph and arbitrary injective labeling; no graph-label algebraic compatibility.

proof: The 2^(r+1) flat points annihilate every degree<=r Boolean monomial, giving bounded relation weight independent of the graph's girth.
costs: Explicit finite-field construction with 2^(r+1) labels; special graph-coupled label cost is unknown.
baseline: Graph cycle codes do inherit minimum distance equal to graph girth, but are different objects.
falsifier: A restriction that the evaluation labeling comes from a graph-compatible parity-check/Tanner map; that additional premise is not in P-graph.
unresolved: Whether a special graph-coupled labeling can have large relation distance remains UNKNOWN.

claim: The P-graph post-switch endpoint-distance rejection filter preserves logarithmic girth, and an exact-radius filter can preserve the source girth, conditional on the imported OA178 switch law and seed guarantees.
quantifiers: Fixed d>=3 and sufficiently large even n in the source construction; M=ceil(n^(1/3+10a)) switches and radius g_n=floor(10^-7 log_{d-1} n), with a=10^-4.

inputs.supplied: Source graph with girth g0, switch-slot pair pointwise law, pairwise-independent seed, and exact rational spectral contrast test.
inputs.acquired: Enumerated seed passing filter and source checks.

proof: Same-draw and cross-draw pair bounds plus a union bound make the filter failure o(1); a cycle decomposition handles arbitrarily many inserted edges.
costs: Enumerates P^2 seeds, O_d(n^2) BFS preprocessing and O(M^2) distance checks per seed; this is polynomial but large.
baseline: Paredes 2021 and the imported OA178 source construction; this audit validates only the added filter conditional on that source.
falsifier: An allowed source switch configuration meeting the filter while creating a cycle shorter than the claimed radius.
unresolved: Imported high-moment, resolvent, concentration, exact repair, and source bit-complexity proof remain unvalidated.

claim: A finite d-regular graph of girth g has empirical adjacency spectral measure within W1 distance 2d/sqrt(g-1) of the Kesten-McKay law; local tree views and bulk spectral convergence need not control connectivity or lambda_2.
quantifiers: Fixed d>=3 and finite simple d-regular graph with g>=3; paired infinite sequence additionally assumes cited LPS and MSS existence theorems.

inputs.supplied: Adjacency spectrum support in [-d,d] and girth g.
inputs.acquired: No numerical spectrum; proof uses exact moments, Bernstein approximation, and cited graph existence results for the pair.

proof: Closed walks of length <g match the universal d-regular tree. Degree-(g-1) Bernstein approximation of 1-Lipschitz functions gives the W1 bound. A disconnected double copy and a connected Ramanujan 2-lift have the same fixed-radius tree balls but a constant lambda_2 gap.
costs: The measure bound is a proof from graph access only. The specific 2-lift is existential under MSS; a signing/acquisition algorithm is not instantiated.
baseline: McKay's 1981 limiting law and LPS/MSS constructions.
falsifier: A closed-walk count disagreement at some length below girth, or failure of the cited LPS/MSS hypotheses for the paired family.
unresolved: Novelty and priority are unknown; no construction beyond the cited existence results is claimed.

claim: For rational x in the relative interior of a face F and rational h in lin(F-F), the two maximal endpoints x+t_+h and x-t_-h support a two-point law with exact mean x; if c^T h=0 it also preserves the linear cost in conditional expectation.
quantifiers: Any rational polytope face, rational interior point, and nonzero rational tangent direction; both endpoint parameters are positive and chosen maximally within F.

inputs.supplied: Exact face endpoints and a tangent direction h; active cost equality c^T h=0 when required.
inputs.acquired: Exact rational endpoint parameters and the two branch probabilities.

proof: Assign mass t_-/(t_++t_-) to x+t_+h and t_+/(t_++t_-) to x-t_-h; the displacement expectation and conditional cost change are zero. Each endpoint lies on a proper subface.
costs: The algebraic update is rational if endpoint parameters are rational; endpoint acquisition and bit growth depend on the polytope oracle and are not bounded by this lemma.
baseline: Lovett-Meka and matroid partial-rounding methods give partial points but not this exact law with a pathwise discrepancy charge on every branch.
falsifier: A direct violation of the displacement or cost expectation identity for legal positive endpoint parameters.
unresolved: No general face-tangent direction engine with polynomial bit complexity, intrinsic progress, and a summable all-branch feature bound is established.

claim: For centered cube rounding with unit Euclidean feature columns, the Gram-Schmidt Walk followed by rejection on a sign-symmetric good event and an independent global sign yields an exact-mean all-supported bounded law; a rational threshold R at least sqrt(80 log(4m)) gives acceptance probability at least one half under the cited subgaussian tail.
quantifiers: Mean x0=0 only; m feature rows and column norms at most one. The rejection event is invariant under global sign reversal.

inputs.supplied: Cube, centered mean, rational feature matrix and threshold.
inputs.acquired: One accepted Gram-Schmidt Walk sample; expected retries at most two at the stated threshold.

proof: Conditioning the symmetric walk law on a sign-invariant event preserves sign symmetry; a final fair global sign makes the mean zero, and every accepted output lies in the event.
costs: Expected O(1) walk calls; the cited walk uses O(n(n+m)^omega) arithmetic operations. Finite-bit sampling is not established here.
baseline: Gram-Schmidt Walk subgaussian rounding and Banaszczyk vector balancing.
falsifier: Failure of the claimed subgaussian tail or a non-sign-invariant acceptance event; neither would establish a general-face result.
unresolved: Does not extend by this argument to arbitrary noncentral means, matroid faces, or arbitrary Boolean polytopes.

claim: A finite H2-prefix-chain example shows that naive compression to arbitrary laminar chain cuts cannot cover every near-minimum cut with a constant number of chain cuts: at n=128 one near-minimum cut requires 126 chain cuts, although a path tree crosses each chain cut once.
quantifiers: The exact constructed finite instances n=16 and n=128 only; no asymptotic universal lower bound on all algorithms or trees is claimed.

inputs.supplied: The explicit H2 prefix instance, candidate interval family, and tree constructed in the leaf script.
inputs.acquired: Exact edge and cut counts from enumeration.

proof: The finite checker enumerates intervals and counts chain-cut coverage; n=16 exhaustively verifies the listed cut parameters, and n=128 gives the 126-cut witness.
costs: Bounded explicit enumeration; artifacts and captured output are in leaf 19.
baseline: Klein-Olver-Yeoh, Thin Trees for Near Minimum Cuts, arXiv:2605.12669v1, whose careful eight-cut coverage is not contradicted.
falsifier: The exact interval/cut counts in the explicit instance fail, or the candidate cut is not near-minimum under the leaf's definitions.
unresolved: Only a finite obstruction to naive arbitrary-laminar compression; no new theorem or general negative result survives.

claim: For K_1,...,K_k linear subspaces of F_2^n with intersection {0}, if every two-dimensional U has dim(U intersect K_i)=1 for at least one i, then n<=2k-1 and the associated injective coset code has size 2^n<=4^k/2.
quantifiers: Every n>=1, k>=1, and finite family of binary linear subspaces satisfying the two listed conditions.

inputs.supplied: The explicit subspaces K_i and their coset-code representation.
inputs.acquired: Subspace intersections, residual affine covers, and an irredundant-cover rank certificate; the proof does not claim efficient acquisition.

proof: The coordinate condition makes the residual uncovered set sum-free. Pairing it with a translate gives an affine cover; Brouwer's binary affine-cover rank inequality charges dimension to disjoint batches of kernels, yielding n<=2k-1.
costs: Existence proof only. Given bases, Gaussian elimination checks subspace intersections; direct verification of all 2-planes costs enumeration. The source-reported private-point cover certificate has size at most k^2; no polynomial-time finder or bit bound is supplied.
baseline: Naslund-Sawin's fixed-alphabet clean-triple-free word bound is semantically related but does not directly cover varying quotient alphabets or yield a uniform base as alphabet size varies.
falsifier: An explicit family satisfying both conditions with n>=2k, or an exact failure of the affine-cover rank recursion.
unresolved: The stronger n<=k bound, a linear-in-k original-kernel certificate, the q>2 extension beyond hyperplane kernels, and representation from unrestricted clean-triple-free word families remain UNKNOWN.
